facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: Three qualifications bound the view. First, Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure that adds back equity compensation and related taxes (293 million over the last twelve months, 34.3% of the 853 million); on operating income plus depreciation and amortization, total debt is 5.10x. Second, net debt and free cash flow flatter cash available after dilution management: 77 million of tax on net share settlement and 60 million of buybacks sit in financing in nine months 2026, and nine-month operating cash flow includes a working-capital inflow of 64 million against an outflow of 76 million a year earlier. Third, the 2027 convertible notes are convertible in the quarter ending 2026-12-31 and were worth 141 million more on an if-converted basis than their principal, so settlement terms can add to the cash need. Covenant levels, guarantor lists and executed documents are not supplied, so no covenant headroom is shown.

facts.label: Definition review
facts.text: - Total debt: the debt note prints Total Debt at carrying amount, net of unamortized discount: 2,799 at 2026-09-30 (page:11). The principal is the sum of the series, 2,829, calculated here. Operating lease liabilities, the capped calls and letters of credit are outside both figures. This module uses the printed carrying total for ratios and says so in each basis cell. - EBITDA, three definitions held apart. (1) The company prints no unadjusted EBITDA; operating income plus depreciation and amortization is calculated here as 549 for the last twelve months. (2) Company-defined Adjusted EBITDA is net income before depreciation and amortization, equity-based compensation and related taxes, interest, other income or expense, taxes, non-recurring items and other items "not indicative of our core operating performance" (Q3 rel page:8). The items in the reconciliation are those in the table above. (3) The covenant EBITDA in the revolver is "Consolidated EBITDA" as defined in the credit agreement (Q3 10-Q page:42), which is not supplied, so it may differ from both. - Equity compensation: the reconciliation adds back "Equity-based compensation and related taxes" of 345 in FY2025, while the cash flow statement shows equity-based compensation expense of 335; the 10 difference is the related-taxes component implied by the two statements, and the pack does not define it. - Free cash flow: net cash from operating activities less purchases of property and equipment and site and software development costs (Q3 rel page:9). It is before debt service principal, before tax paid on net share settlement and before buybacks, which are financing lines. - Cash interest: "Cash paid for interest on long-term debt" in the cash flow supplemental information (Q3 10-Q page:5). It is gross of interest income, which is 30 for nine months 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:9). - Liquidity: the 10-Q table is cash plus short-term investments and excludes the revolver (page:39); the releases state a larger "total liquidity" including revolver availability (Q3 rel page:1). Both are shown and labelled below. - LTM: last twelve months equals the 10-K year plus the current year-to-date less the prior-year year-to-date, calculated here and labelled as derived.

(2) Company-defined Adjusted EBITDA is net income before depreciation and amortization, equity-based compensation and related taxes, interest, other income or expense, taxes, non-recurring items and other items "not indicative of our core operating performance" (Q3 rel page:8). The items in the reconciliation are those in the table above. (3) The covenant EBITDA in the revolver is "Consolidated EBITDA" as defined in the credit agreement (Q3 10-Q page:42), which is not supplied, so it may differ from both.

- Equity compensation: the reconciliation adds back "Equity-based compensation and related taxes" of 345 in FY2025, while the cash flow statement shows equity-based compensation expense of 335; the 10 difference is the related-taxes component implied by the two statements, and the pack does not define it.

- Free cash flow: net cash from operating activities less purchases of property and equipment and site and software development costs (Q3 rel page:9). It is before debt service principal, before tax paid on net share settlement and before buybacks, which are financing lines.

- Cash interest: "Cash paid for interest on long-term debt" in the cash flow supplemental information (Q3 10-Q page:5). It is gross of interest income, which is 30 for nine months 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:9).

- Liquidity: the 10-Q table is cash plus short-term investments and excludes the revolver (page:39); the releases state a larger "total liquidity" including revolver availability (Q3 rel page:1). Both are shown and labelled below.
- LTM: last twelve months equals the 10-K year plus the current year-to-date less the prior-year year-to-date, calculated here and labelled as derived.

facts.label: Earnings quality and definition risks
facts.text: - Adjusted EBITDA bridge, last twelve months to Q3 2026: operating income 283 plus D&A 266 plus equity compensation and related taxes 293 plus impairment, restructuring and other charges 11 equals 853 (calculated). Equity compensation is therefore 34.3% of Adjusted EBITDA, against 46.4% in FY2025 (345 of 743). The fall reflects both lower equity compensation and higher Adjusted EBITDA. - Non-cash versus cash: 77 of tax on net share settlement was paid in cash in nine months 2026 and 89 in FY2025, outside operating cash flow and free cash flow. Shares withheld for that purpose are a cash cost of equity pay that the Adjusted EBITDA add-back does not show. - A one-time benefit is in the prior-year base: the Q3 10-Q says nine-month cost of goods sold rose partly because of "the absence of a one-time benefit of $38 million related to a resolution on the valuation of duties" in Q1 2025 (page:35). The prior-year nine-month Adjusted EBITDA therefore includes that benefit, and the reconciliation has no add-back for it; the last-twelve-month measure removes the nine-month 2025 period. FY2025 cost of goods sold also carries a 45 benefit from customs duty examinations (10-K page:133), which is likewise not adjusted out. - Q3 2026 selling, operations, technology, general and administrative expense includes "costs associated with a legal settlement" (Q3 10-Q page:33), not quantified. - Restructuring and impairment add-backs are 26 in nine months 2026 against 91 a year earlier, and none in Q3 2026 (page:3); the 24 in 2026 is a loss on termination of an operating lease for a logistics facility (page:8). - Segment concentration: U.S. Adjusted EBITDA of 683 over nine months 2026 against a loss of 54 in International, so earnings quality depends on U.S. execution (Q3 rel page:11).

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Wayfair Inc. is a Delaware-incorporated, Boston-headquartered online home-goods retailer listed on the New York Stock Exchange (10-K page:1, page:9). It has no financial sponsor and the pack contains no merger, acquisition or sponsor transaction. The business sells through six brand storefronts, ships most orders directly from roughly 20 thousand suppliers' warehouses, and is adding its own warehouses, delivery network and a small physical store base (10-K page:9-14). The U.S. segment was 88% of FY2025 net revenue (10-K page:10). Ownership is public but control is concentrated: Class B stock carries ten votes per share, and at year-end 2025 the co-founders and their affiliates held about 18.3% of the economic interest and 67.4% of the voting power (10-K page:62).

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: For a creditor the transaction history that matters is capital structure change, not a deal. Since October 2024 the company issued four series of fixed-rate senior secured notes through its subsidiary Wayfair LLC totalling 2,600 million, entered into an amended and restated 500 million revolving credit facility, and used cash and the new issues to retire convertible notes that carried lower coupons and whose if-converted value exceeded principal at 2025-12-31 (10-K page:130). The effect, set out in the accepted financial base, is lower total debt and a maturity profile with nothing due in the rest of 2026 or in 2028 and 229 million due in 2027, at the price of higher fixed interest and a secured claim stack that ranks ahead of the remaining unsecured convertible notes. Five qualifications bound the view: the executed indentures and credit agreement are not supplied; two of the four issues have no stated use of proceeds in the pack; the 2026 proxy statement, which carries board and compensation detail, is not supplied; no credit rating is supplied; and the pack gives no management guidance. Nothing after the cutoff is used.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: New debt issues in the period covered are four. First, 800 million of 7.250% senior secured notes due 2029 were issued on 2024-10-08 (10-K page:121). Second, 700 million of 7.750% notes due 2030 were issued on 2025-03-13 alongside the amended and restated credit agreement that provides the 500 million revolver maturing 2030-03-13 (10-K page:119, page:121). The 10-K states the use: on 2025-03-14 the company repurchased 578 million of 2026 convertible notes in connection with the issuance, and on 2025-05-09 it used the remaining proceeds with cash to repurchase 80 million of 2025 notes and 118 million of 2026 notes (10-K page:128). Third, 700 million of 6.750% notes due 2032 were issued on 2025-11-07 (10-K page:121); the pack does not state a use of proceeds, and the repurchase of 210 million of 2027 notes on 2025-11-12 for 375 million cash (10-K page:128) is close in time but is not linked to the issue by the filing, so no link is asserted. Fourth, 400 million of 7.125% notes due 2034 were issued on 2026-05-18, and the company used the proceeds with cash on hand on 2026-06-29 to settle the remaining 444 million of 2028 convertible notes after a redemption notice of 2026-05-14 (Q3 10-Q page:41, page:14-15). For the 2029 series the pack gives no use of proceeds.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The liquidity effect of the 2026 actions, from the accepted financial base, is that nine-month 2026 net cash on debt principal and extinguishment was 585 while operating cash flow was 506 and cash fell by 438 to 1,038. The effect on leverage is that carrying total debt fell from 3,272 at year-end 2025 to 2,799 and total debt to company-defined Adjusted EBITDA was 3.28x on the last-twelve-month figure of 853. The mechanism for creditors is as follows. Replacing convertible notes with coupons of 3.50% and below by secured notes at 6.750% to 7.750% raises fixed interest; the accepted base puts stated coupons on outstanding debt at about 195 a year against last-twelve-month cash interest of 170. It lengthens maturities, since the earliest remaining maturity is the 229 million 2027 convertible notes. It adds secured claims that share first-priority liens with the revolver, while the remaining convertible notes are unsecured and structurally subordinated. Convertible notes retired for cash above principal convert dilution into a cash cost: cash paid, including accrued interest and fees, was 375 for 210 of principal in 2025 and 247 for 145 in 2026 (Calculations), with extinguishment losses of 165 and 102 equal to the difference to carrying value. Shares were also issued in settlement: 0.9 million on the 2027 notes and 4.5 million on the 2028 notes (Q3 10-Q page:14-15). The 2027 notes themselves became convertible for the quarter ending 2026-12-31 and the filing says conversion may be settled in cash, shares or a combination at the company's election (Q3 10-Q page:13), so the remaining unsecured claim carries a cash call that the company controls through the form of settlement. Recovery prospects appear here as a mechanic only: secured and unsecured claims have different positions against the same asset base, and the pack gives no valuation or recovery analysis.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Wayfair Inc. is a better credit than it was two years ago, but it is still a thin-margin, discretionary-demand retailer whose leverage looks moderate only on management's own earnings measure. The strongest support is deleveraging: total debt fell to USD 2,799 million and total debt to Adjusted EBITDA to 3.28x from 6.88x in FY2024, with USD 1,098 million of cash and investments, an undrawn revolver and no maturity before September 2027. The weakest point is earnings quality: Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 293 million of equity compensation, and on operating income plus depreciation and amortization the ratio is 5.10x. What decides the outcome is whether U.S. order growth keeps converting into earnings faster than fixed interest is rising.

citations.quote: Wayfair Inc. is a better credit than it was two years ago, but it is still a thin-margin, discretionary-demand retailer whose leverage looks moderate only on management's own earnings measure. The strongest support is deleveraging: total debt fell to USD 2,799 million and total debt to Adjusted EBITDA to 3.28x from 6.88x in FY2024, with USD 1,098 million of cash and investments, an undrawn revolver and no maturity before September 2027. The weakest point is earnings quality: Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 293 million of equity compensation, and on operating income plus depreciation and amortization the ratio is 5.10x. What decides the outcome is whether U.S. order growth keeps converting into earnings faster than fixed interest is rising.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, Wayfair has cut its debt and raised its earnings at the same time. Carrying total debt is USD 2,799 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 3,118 million at 2024-12-31, while last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is USD 853 million against USD 453 million in FY2024 [CP-1 handoff, leverage and metrics tables]. Total debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 3.28x and net debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 1.99x (Documentary Fact for the inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the improvement being earnings-led, since debt fell 10.2% and Adjusted EBITDA rose 88.3%).

citations.quote: First, Wayfair has cut its debt and raised its earnings at the same time. Carrying total debt is USD 2,799 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 3,118 million at 2024-12-31, while last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is USD 853 million against USD 453 million in FY2024 [CP-1 handoff, leverage and metrics tables]. Total debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 3.28x and net debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 1.99x (Documentary Fact for the inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the improvement being earnings-led, since debt fell 10.2% and Adjusted EBITDA rose 88.3%).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Second, liquidity is ample against the visible maturities. Wayfair holds USD 1,038 million of cash and USD 60 million of short-term investments, has USD 418 million of undrawn revolver after letters of credit, and owes USD 229 million of convertible notes in September 2027 and USD 800 million of secured notes in October 2029 [CP-1 handoff, liquidity and maturity tables]. Cash and investments cover the 2027 principal 4.8 times (Calculations). The remaining unsecured notes are convertible during the quarter ending 2026-12-31 with an if-converted excess over principal of USD 141 million, and the company may settle in cash, shares or both, so the cash call is within its control [CP-1 handoff, debt schedule; CP-1A handoff, transaction summary] (Documentary Fact).

Cash and investments cover the 2027 principal 4.8 times (Calculations). The remaining unsecured notes are convertible during the quarter ending 2026-12-31 with an if-converted excess over principal of USD 141 million, and the company may settle in cash, shares or both, so the cash call is within its control [CP-1 handoff, debt schedule; CP-1A handoff, transaction summary] (Documentary Fact).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Third, the quality of the earnings measure decides how comfortable the leverage is. Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 293 million of equity-based compensation and related taxes over the last twelve months, which is 34.3% of Adjusted EBITDA, and the company also paid USD 77 million of tax on net share settlement and USD 60 million of buybacks through financing in nine months 2026 [CP-1 handoff, definition review]. On operating income plus depreciation and amortization of USD 549 million, total debt is 5.10x and net debt 3.10x; operating income of USD 283 million covers net interest expense of USD 156 million 1.81x (Calculations) (Analyst Interpretation).

citations.quote: Third, the quality of the earnings measure decides how comfortable the leverage is. Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 293 million of equity-based compensation and related taxes over the last twelve months, which is 34.3% of Adjusted EBITDA, and the company also paid USD 77 million of tax on net share settlement and USD 60 million of buybacks through financing in nine months 2026 [CP-1 handoff, definition review]. On operating income plus depreciation and amortization of USD 549 million, total debt is 5.10x and net debt 3.10x; operating income of USD 283 million covers net interest expense of USD 156 million 1.81x (Calculations) (Analyst Interpretation).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Fourth, the cost of debt is rising even as the balance falls. Wayfair issued four fixed-rate secured series totalling USD 2,600 million since October 2024 and retired convertible notes with coupons of 3.50% and below, so stated coupons on USD 2,829 million of principal now total about USD 195 million a year against last-twelve-month cash interest of USD 170 million; Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 5.02x and run-rate coupons 4.36x [CP-1 handoff, interest cover; CP-1A handoff, transaction summary] (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation).

facts.text: Fifth, the business is volume-led and U.S.-concentrated. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. The first strength is deleveraging with earnings growth: last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 853 million is up from USD 743 million in FY2025 and USD 453 million in FY2024, and total debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 3.28x from 4.40x and 6.88x [CP-1 handoff] (Documentary Fact). The second is liquidity: USD 1,098 million of cash and short-term investments and USD 418 million of undrawn revolver exceed the USD 229 million due before 2029, which cash and investments alone cover 4.8 times (Calculations), and last-twelve-month free cash flow is USD 476 million, 55.8% of Adjusted EBITDA [CP-1 handoff] (Documentary Fact; the multiple is Analyst Interpretation). The third is a longer maturity profile: the 2026 and 2028 convertible notes are gone, the earliest remaining maturity is USD 229 million in September 2027, and the secured notes mature in 2029, 2030, 2032 and 2034 [CP-1 handoff, maturity table] (Documentary Fact). The fourth is repeat demand and growth: repeat customers placed 80.0% of Q3 2026 orders and net revenue rose 9.7% in the quarter, which supports revenue durability [CP-1A handoff; CP-1 handoff] (Documentary Fact; the release KPIs are management-calculated). The fifth is market access: the secured notes carry fair values between 98.9% and 102.9% of principal at 2026-09-30 (CP-1 handoff, debt schedule), consistent with continued access to secured debt markets (Analyst Interpretation).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. The first weakness is thin and adjusted earnings: net income over the last twelve months is a loss of USD 160 million, operating income plus depreciation and amortization is USD 549 million against Adjusted EBITDA of USD 853 million, and the stockholders' deficit is USD 2,804 million [CP-1 handoff] (Documentary Fact). The second is rising fixed interest, as set out in the fourth key finding, which leaves less room if earnings slip [CP-1 handoff; CP-1A handoff] (Analyst Interpretation). The third is demand and concentration risk: a discretionary category, 88% U.S. revenue, a loss-making International segment and a single small-parcel carrier [CP-1A handoff, Company and operating model] (Documentary Fact). The fourth is working-capital and seasonality sensitivity: first-quarter operating cash flow was negative in both years printed, and the 2026 working-capital inflow may not repeat [CP-1 handoff] (Analyst Interpretation). The fifth is that the claim stack is secured-heavy: secured notes are 91.9% of principal and share first-priority liens with the revolver, so the unsecured convertible notes rank behind them and structurally behind subsidiary liabilities, which matters for any loss given default analysis that later modules perform (mechanic only) [CP-1 handoff; CP-1A handoff] (Documentary Fact). The sixth is control and information: founder voting control, no covenant ratio reported, no ratings and no guidance mean that downside protection cannot be measured (Insufficient Information; the missing datapoints are the covenant definition and reported ratio, executed indentures, the proxy statement and ratings, as set out in Gaps).

facts.text: The strongest evidence for a better credit view than the Medium-confidence synthesis is that Q3 2026 operating income of 106 is up from 38, Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA margin of 6.9% is up from 6.7%, orders delivered rose 12.2%, last-twelve-month free cash flow of 476 is 55.8% of Adjusted EBITDA, and liquidity of 1,516 including the revolver is large against 229 due in 2027. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The downside chain, with observable triggers, starts with a slowdown in U.S. demand (initiating condition). The first operational break would be falling orders delivered or lower average order value, which the release reports each quarter, forcing more advertising per order. The financial transmission is lower Adjusted EBITDA and a reversal of the 64 working-capital inflow as payables of 1,213 unwind against inventories of 89. The consequences are lower cash than the 1,038 held, less cover than 5.02x, and higher leverage, with the arithmetic reference points that LTM Adjusted EBITDA at the FY2025 level of 743 gives total debt of 3.77x and at the FY2024 level of 453 gives 6.18x (Calculations; these are reference levels, not forecasts). Refinancing then matters from 2029, when 800 of secured notes mature at market rates. Triggers to watch: quarterly orders and average order value, Adjusted EBITDA margin against 6.9%, cash against 1,038, the settlement election on the 2027 notes, and covenant certificates when obtained.

Issuer: Wayfair Inc. (issuer id w; NYSE ticker W; Delaware registrant, SEC file number 001-36666). As-of date: 2026-11-05. Evidence cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The pack supports the requested work on Wayfair Inc. through the third quarter of 2026, with bounded limits. Executed debt documents, covenant ratios and guarantor lists are not supplied, so legal terms rest on filing summaries. | Medium | The credit agreement, indentures and reported covenant ratio are not in the pack; the covenant level is known only from filing text. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The annual report, three quarterly reports and three releases cover FY2025 through Q3 2026 in US dollars, with statements, debt note and liquidity table located. | A financial base, debt picture and liquidity view can be built from filed statements without outside data. | High |

| Convertible notes are issued by the parent, while the secured notes and the revolver sit at a subsidiary; guarantors are not named in full. | Ranking of each claim and structural subordination of the convertible notes need the executed documents, which are not supplied. | Medium |

| One maintenance test is named, a senior secured leverage cap, and the reported ratio and headroom are not printed. | Covenant headroom cannot be measured from the pack; only the stated compliance can be carried forward. | High |

| The 2027 convertible notes became convertible for the fourth quarter of 2026, and an equity instrument settled for cash after quarter end. | Cash settlement of conversions and share-repurchase outflows can draw on liquidity; they must be carried as open items. | Medium |

| Ratings, market prices and executed legal documents are not supplied, and the Canadian customs matter appears only in the annual report. | Relative-value and rating-based work cannot proceed, and the customs exposure is not updated after year end. | High |
### Readiness view

The effective source set supports the requested work with limitations. All four consumers are assessed as READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, none CONDITIONAL and none BLOCKED. The audited annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases cover the periods the context names, in the reporting currency, up to the evidence cutoff, and the latest filed report is signed on 2026-11-04. The binding limitations are four. First, no executed legal document is in the pack, so the covenant, guarantor, security and indenture terms rest on filing summaries, and the reported value of the one named financial covenant is not printed. Second, the debt sits at more than one legal entity (parent convertible notes; subsidiary secured notes and revolver) and the guarantor group is not listed, so the claim-by-claim map is incomplete. Third, no fidelity review of the text extraction has been done, and the pack has no slides or images. Fourth, no credit rating, market price or peer data is supplied. None of these prevents the owners from running their methods, but each must be carried forward as stated in the consumer assessment and gaps below.
### Source-by-source assessment

All seven sources identify Wayfair Inc. as the registrant or the announcing company (page:1 of each). No source is blocked, draft, unsigned or an exact duplicate of another. The 10-K is audited; the three 10-Qs are unaudited and condensed. The filed 10-K and 10-Qs control their own facts. The three releases are management claims that must not override the filings, and each repeats the statements already in the matching 10-Q. Base, amendment, waiver and supplement documents do not arise: no legal document of any kind is in the pack.

### Entity and perimeter

The registrant and reporting entity is Wayfair Inc., with its financial statements stated to be those of "Wayfair Inc. and its wholly-owned subsidiaries" (Q3 10-Q page:6). The context names no borrower, parent or guarantor, and a search of the sources for "parent" found no corporate parent of Wayfair Inc. Two reportable segments are given, the U.S. and International (Q3 10-Q page:22).
Debt roles as the filings print them:

- Revolver: the 10-K says "Wayfair LLC, a subsidiary of Wayfair, as borrower", with Wayfair and "certain of its subsidiaries" as the Guarantors, and first-priority liens on substantially all assets of the Borrower and the Guarantors (10-K page:119). Administrative agent and collateral agent is Citibank, N.A. (page:119).

- Senior Secured Notes: Wayfair LLC is the Issuer of the 2029, 2030, 2032 and 2034 secured notes, under indentures that name guarantors "including Wayfair" (10-K page:121-122; Q2 10-Q page:12 for the 2034 series; the Q3 10-Q page:41 repeats that Wayfair LLC issued the 2034 series). The notes rank pari passu with the revolver on the same first-priority liens (10-K page:130).

- Convertible Notes: the 10-K says "The Convertible Notes are general senior unsecured obligations of Wayfair" and "structurally subordinated to all existing and future indebtedness and liabilities of" Wayfair's subsidiaries (10-K page:130); the indentures "also include Wayfair LLC, as guarantor" (page:125). Only the 2027 Notes remain outstanding at 2026-09-30 (Q3 10-Q page:10-11).

Unresolved distinctions, kept as gaps and not as conclusions: the "certain of its subsidiaries" that guarantee are not listed; the Q3 10-Q does not repeat the guarantor description for the revolver or the notes; the restricted versus unrestricted subsidiary split used in the secured-note indentures is not supplied; and no guarantor or non-guarantor financial information is in the pack (search below).
### Period basis and version relationships

All seven sources are on one perimeter (consolidated Wayfair Inc.), one currency (USD, millions) and one accounting basis (GAAP, with management non-GAAP measures labelled as such). A search of all seven sources for "discontinued operation" and "held for sale" returned no hit, and no restated or recast statement was found (the 10-K hits for "restated" are the amended and restated credit agreement and exhibit titles), so no perimeter change is evident. For net revenue, the prior-year quarterly columns in the Q1 and Q2 reports sum to the nine-month 2025 amount in the Q3 report (tie-out below); other prior-year lines were not re-tested.

Discrete periods available: Q1 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:2, release page:2), Q2 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:2, release page:2), Q3 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:3) and the nine months to 2026-09-30, each with a prior-year comparative column; FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023 annual columns (10-K page:100). Q4 2025 as a stand-alone quarter is not printed anywhere in the pack: no fourth-quarter release or report is supplied, so it is derivable only as FY2025 less nine months 2025, which is downstream work and is not done here. A last-twelve-months view to 2026-09-30 can be built from FY2025, nine months 2026 and nine months 2025 for net revenue, Adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow and cash interest; each of those components is printed.

Quarter versus year-to-date: the Q3 report prints both three-month and nine-month columns side by side (page:3), and the Q3 cash flow statement is nine months only (page:4). Quarterly cash flow therefore needs the Q2 report's six-month column to be subtracted downstream. Cash paid for interest is printed for each cumulative period (Q1 10-Q page:4; Q2 10-Q page:4; Q3 10-Q page:5; 10-K page:101). Cash taxes paid are not printed in the interim reports; the 10-K gives FY2025 only, as state and foreign payments (page:137).

Management claims to carry with attribution only: the Q3 release calls the 6.9% Adjusted EBITDA Margin "our best Q3 result since 2020" and Q3 "our strongest quarter of growth in the post-pandemic period" (page:1), and the Q2 release headline reports "Strongest Free Cash Flow Since 2020" (page:1). The pack holds only the current and prior-year quarters, so these multi-year comparisons cannot be checked and are not relied on.
### Debt and liquidity evidence present

The Q3 10-Q debt note (page:10-17) gives, at 2026-09-30 and 2025-12-31, in millions: principal, unamortized discount and net carrying amount for the revolver (nil drawn), 2026 Notes, 2027 Notes, 2028 Notes, 2029, 2030, 2032 and 2034 Secured Notes. Total debt carrying amount is 2,799 (2025-12-31: 3,272), of which short-term 227 and long-term 2,572 (page:11). Coupons, maturity dates, effective rates and interest dates for the four secured series and the 2027 Notes are tabulated (page:11), as are conversion terms for the 2027 Notes (initial conversion price $63.45, free convertibility from June 15, 2027; page:12) and the capped calls (page:16). Fair values at 2026-09-30 are printed for each outstanding series (page:15). The 10-K and the Q2 10-Q give the issuance terms of the secured notes (10-K page:121-122; Q2 10-Q page:12).

Revolver: US$500 million, matures March 13, 2030, no loans outstanding, and US$82 million of letters of credit (mostly lease security) reduce availability (Q3 10-Q page:11, page:39). The 10-K also says the maturity is "subject to a springing earlier maturity in certain circumstances" without stating the trigger (page:119). Margin at 2025-12-31 is 1.25% for Term SOFR loans (10-K page:120); no later margin is printed.

Liquidity: the 10-Q table shows cash and cash equivalents of 1,038 and short-term investments of 60, total 1,098, which excludes the revolver (page:39). The release states "total liquidity was $1.5 billion, including availability under our revolving credit facility" (release page:1). All inputs for a liquidity build by component are printed: cash, short-term investments, revolver size, letters of credit, and the cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash line of the cash flow statement (page:4).

The 2027 Notes: conditional conversion was triggered in the quarter ended 2026-09-30, so they are convertible during the quarter ending 2026-12-31 (page:13, page:41); the if-converted value exceeded principal by 141 (page:15); settlement may be in cash, shares or a combination at the company's election (page:13). This is evidence for downstream cash-need analysis, not a conclusion here.

Other claims outside the debt note that are located: operating lease liabilities of 864 non-current (page:2) and lease obligations of 110 for leases not yet commenced (page:8, page:45); a logistics lease termination that reduced lease obligations by 138 (page:8); purchase obligations of 649 at 2025-12-31 for software licence and freight commitments (10-K page:84, page:132); the 10-K contractual obligations table at 2025-12-31 (page:83-84), which the Q3 report says has had no material change other than the financing transactions (page:45). No finance lease arrangements were material at 2025-12-31 (10-K page:106). Retirement benefits are a defined-contribution 401(k) plan (10-K page:133). No pension, factoring, supply-chain finance or rating-agency item appears (search results in Gaps).
### Quarter, subsequent events and contingencies

Located for the latest quarter and after, to the cutoff: the 2026 Notes matured on August 15, 2026 and 39 was paid in cash (Q3 10-Q page:13); the 2027 Notes conversion trigger above; share repurchases of 60 under the 2020 program (page:18); an equity instrument for 60 that "was settled on October 28, 2026, resulting in a cash settlement of $64 million" (page:18, page:42), a post-quarter-end event dated before the cutoff; and Class A shares outstanding of 115,862,125 at October 28, 2026 (page:1). Earlier in 2026: repurchases and redemptions of the 2028 and 2027 Notes with loss on debt extinguishment, and the $400 million 2034 Secured Notes issued May 18, 2026 (page:14-15, page:41). Litigation: ordinary-course matters, accruals recorded and "fully insured for a majority of these matters" (page:17); no amounts are quantified there, and the Q3 report says no material change in risk factors (page:55). The Canada Border Services Agency review and customs examinations are described in the 10-K only (page:132-133) and are not mentioned in any 2026 report. Nothing dated after 2026-11-05 is relied on; the Q3 release and report are dated 2026-11-04, one day before the as-of date, and nothing dated between is supplied.

Tables arrive as flattened text, and column headers were checked against the period labels printed beside each table. The pack contains no slides, images or charts, so no image-content coverage is claimed. A successful extraction is not a fidelity review of every table, and none is claimed.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Reported figures support a complete financial base to the third quarter of 2026. On company-defined earnings, total debt is 3.28x and net debt 1.99x, with interest cover of 5.02x. Earnings quality and covenant headroom carry limits. | Medium | Earnings are company-adjusted and add back equity compensation; covenant definitions and market data are not supplied, so headroom and relative value cannot be measured. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is 853 million against 453 million in FY2024, while total debt fell from 3,118 million to 2,799 million. | Total debt to Adjusted EBITDA improved from 6.88x to 3.28x, driven more by earnings growth than by debt reduction. | High |

| Adjusted EBITDA adds back 293 million of equity compensation and related taxes in the last twelve months; operating income plus depreciation and amortization is 549 million. | On that unadjusted measure total debt is 5.10x, so leverage is sensitive to whether equity pay is treated as a cost. | Medium |

| Cash is 1,038 million and the undrawn revolver is 418 million after letters of credit, against 229 million of convertible notes due in 2027. | Cash exceeds the 2027 notes, but conversion settlement terms leave the cash need open. | Medium |

| Last-twelve-month free cash flow is 476 million, but 77 million of share-settlement tax and 60 million of buybacks sit in financing in nine months 2026. | Cash after dilution management is lower than free cash flow, and nine-month operating cash flow benefited from a working-capital inflow. | Medium |

| Interest cover is 5.02x on last-twelve-month cash interest, but stated coupons on debt outstanding at 30 September 2026 total about 195 million a year. | Cover on run-rate coupons is lower at 4.36x; the 2034 notes replaced lower-coupon convertibles, so cash interest is rising. | Medium |
### Financial base view

The reported base is complete for the requested use: audited FY2024 and FY2025 annual statements, three quarterly reports and three releases give statements of operations, balance sheets and cash flows for every period needed, in one currency, one perimeter and one accounting basis, with prior-year comparatives. On the company's own Adjusted EBITDA, last-twelve-month earnings to Q3 2026 are 853 million, up from 743 million in FY2025 and 453 million in FY2024, and total debt at carrying amount fell from 3,272 million at 2025-12-31 to 2,799 million at 2026-09-30. That moves total debt to Adjusted EBITDA from 4.40x to 3.28x and net debt to Adjusted EBITDA from 2.33x to 1.99x; the improvement since FY2024 is mainly earnings growth, since debt fell by 10.2% while Adjusted EBITDA rose by 88.3%. Cash and short-term investments are 1,098 million, the revolver is undrawn, and the capital structure is now all fixed-rate: 2,600 million of senior secured notes and 229 million of 2027 convertible notes, with no maturity before 2027.

Three qualifications bound the view. First, Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure that adds back equity compensation and related taxes (293 million over the last twelve months, 34.3% of the 853 million); on operating income plus depreciation and amortization, total debt is 5.10x. Second, net debt and free cash flow flatter cash available after dilution management: 77 million of tax on net share settlement and 60 million of buybacks sit in financing in nine months 2026, and nine-month operating cash flow includes a working-capital inflow of 64 million against an outflow of 76 million a year earlier. Third, the 2027 convertible notes are convertible in the quarter ending 2026-12-31 and were worth 141 million more on an if-converted basis than their principal, so settlement terms can add to the cash need. Covenant levels, guarantor lists and executed documents are not supplied, so no covenant headroom is shown.

### Liquidity and cash flow reading

- Liquidity at 2026-09-30: cash 1,038 plus short-term investments 60 is 1,098 (Q3 10-Q page:39); with 418 of undrawn revolver after letters of credit, the arithmetic total is 1,516, consistent with the release wording of a total liquidity of 1.5 billion (Q3 rel page:1). Cash fell from 1,476 at 2025-12-31 by 438 over nine months while operating cash flow was 506, because financing used 782: 245 to extinguish debt, 696 of settlement of long-term debt, 39 at maturity, 77 for tax on net share settlement, 60 of buybacks and 60 for an equity instrument, against 395 of new debt proceeds (Q3 10-Q page:4).

- Debt activity in nine months 2026: net cash paid on debt principal and extinguishment was 585 (980 out less 395 in), and the principal outstanding fell from 3,308 to 2,829 as 39 of 2026 Notes, 251 of 2027 Notes and 589 of 2028 Notes were retired and 400 of 2034 Secured Notes were issued. Loss on debt extinguishment of 102 was charged (page:3); it is outside Adjusted EBITDA.

- Operating cash flow quality: nine-month operating cash flow rose from 332 to 506. The Q3 10-Q attributes 140 of the 174 increase to cash changes in operating assets and liabilities (page:44). Accounts payable of 1,213 against inventories of 89 (page:2) mean the working-capital line is large relative to inventory, and the 64 inflow in nine months 2026 may not repeat.
- Capital expenditure including site and software costs was 1.8% of net revenue in nine months 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:44), consistent with 175 over 9,870.

- Free cash flow was negative in Q1 2026 (106 outflow, Q1 rel page:1) and positive in Q2 2026 (301) and Q3 2026 (136). Free cash flow was also negative in Q1 2025 (139 outflow, Q1 rel page:2), so the first quarter is weak in both years printed.

- Interest: the 2034 Secured Notes at 7.125% replaced 2028 Notes at 3.50% (Q3 10-Q page:41, page:14), which is why the Q3 10-Q says interest expense, net rose by 11 to 42 in Q3 and to 120 from 83 in nine months (page:33, page:38). Stated coupons on the 2,829 of principal outstanding at 2026-09-30 total about 195 a year (calculated), above the 170 of last-twelve-month cash interest and before interest income, which was 30 for nine months (page:9).
### Earnings quality and definition risks

- Adjusted EBITDA bridge, last twelve months to Q3 2026: operating income 283 plus D&A 266 plus equity compensation and related taxes 293 plus impairment, restructuring and other charges 11 equals 853 (calculated). Equity compensation is therefore 34.3% of Adjusted EBITDA, against 46.4% in FY2025 (345 of 743). The fall reflects both lower equity compensation and higher Adjusted EBITDA.

- Non-cash versus cash: 77 of tax on net share settlement was paid in cash in nine months 2026 and 89 in FY2025, outside operating cash flow and free cash flow. Shares withheld for that purpose are a cash cost of equity pay that the Adjusted EBITDA add-back does not show.

- A one-time benefit is in the prior-year base: the Q3 10-Q says nine-month cost of goods sold rose partly because of "the absence of a one-time benefit of $38 million related to a resolution on the valuation of duties" in Q1 2025 (page:35). The prior-year nine-month Adjusted EBITDA therefore includes that benefit, and the reconciliation has no add-back for it; the last-twelve-month measure removes the nine-month 2025 period. FY2025 cost of goods sold also carries a 45 benefit from customs duty examinations (10-K page:133), which is likewise not adjusted out.
- Q3 2026 selling, operations, technology, general and administrative expense includes "costs associated with a legal settlement" (Q3 10-Q page:33), not quantified.

- Restructuring and impairment add-backs are 26 in nine months 2026 against 91 a year earlier, and none in Q3 2026 (page:3); the 24 in 2026 is a loss on termination of an operating lease for a logistics facility (page:8).
- Segment concentration: U.S. Adjusted EBITDA of 683 over nine months 2026 against a loss of 54 in International, so earnings quality depends on U.S. execution (Q3 rel page:11).

Question for this module: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to a creditor of Wayfair Inc., and what do they imply for risk? The reader is a credit committee. Required decision drivers: transaction and ownership structure; business and operating model; credit-relevant history or change. This module gives no peer ranking, no instrument recommendation and no recovery conclusion.

The context file is not issuer evidence: its sector and country fields are user inputs, and its blank sponsor, deal-term, rating and peer fields are Not supplied, never zero.

### Business and transaction view

Wayfair Inc. is a Delaware-incorporated, Boston-headquartered online home-goods retailer listed on the New York Stock Exchange (10-K page:1, page:9). It has no financial sponsor and the pack contains no merger, acquisition or sponsor transaction. The business sells through six brand storefronts, ships most orders directly from roughly 20 thousand suppliers' warehouses, and is adding its own warehouses, delivery network and a small physical store base (10-K page:9-14). The U.S. segment was 88% of FY2025 net revenue (10-K page:10). Ownership is public but control is concentrated: Class B stock carries ten votes per share, and at year-end 2025 the co-founders and their affiliates held about 18.3% of the economic interest and 67.4% of the voting power (10-K page:62).

For a creditor the transaction history that matters is capital structure change, not a deal. Since October 2024 the company issued four series of fixed-rate senior secured notes through its subsidiary Wayfair LLC totalling 2,600 million, entered into an amended and restated 500 million revolving credit facility, and used cash and the new issues to retire convertible notes that carried lower coupons and whose if-converted value exceeded principal at 2025-12-31 (10-K page:130). The effect, set out in the accepted financial base, is lower total debt and a maturity profile with nothing due in the rest of 2026 or in 2028 and 229 million due in 2027, at the price of higher fixed interest and a secured claim stack that ranks ahead of the remaining unsecured convertible notes. Five qualifications bound the view: the executed indentures and credit agreement are not supplied; two of the four issues have no stated use of proceeds in the pack; the 2026 proxy statement, which carries board and compensation detail, is not supplied; no credit rating is supplied; and the pack gives no management guidance. Nothing after the cutoff is used.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

There is no merger, acquisition, sponsor buyout or divestiture transaction in the pack, and the context holds no deal terms, so the transaction type is capital structure refinancing, completed, with no pending transaction. Documentary status is that every debt action below is complete as of the Q3 10-Q signed on 2026-11-04. The issuer of each secured series is Wayfair LLC, a subsidiary of Wayfair Inc., under indentures with the guarantors named therein, including Wayfair Inc., and U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association as trustee and notes collateral agent (10-K page:121-122; Q2 10-Q page:12). The accepted financial base gives the amounts, coupons and maturities, which are not repeated in full here.

New debt issues in the period covered are four. First, 800 million of 7.250% senior secured notes due 2029 were issued on 2024-10-08 (10-K page:121). Second, 700 million of 7.750% notes due 2030 were issued on 2025-03-13 alongside the amended and restated credit agreement that provides the 500 million revolver maturing 2030-03-13 (10-K page:119, page:121). The 10-K states the use: on 2025-03-14 the company repurchased 578 million of 2026 convertible notes in connection with the issuance, and on 2025-05-09 it used the remaining proceeds with cash to repurchase 80 million of 2025 notes and 118 million of 2026 notes (10-K page:128). Third, 700 million of 6.750% notes due 2032 were issued on 2025-11-07 (10-K page:121); the pack does not state a use of proceeds, and the repurchase of 210 million of 2027 notes on 2025-11-12 for 375 million cash (10-K page:128) is close in time but is not linked to the issue by the filing, so no link is asserted. Fourth, 400 million of 7.125% notes due 2034 were issued on 2026-05-18, and the company used the proceeds with cash on hand on 2026-06-29 to settle the remaining 444 million of 2028 convertible notes after a redemption notice of 2026-05-14 (Q3 10-Q page:41, page:14-15). For the 2029 series the pack gives no use of proceeds.

The liquidity effect of the 2026 actions, from the accepted financial base, is that nine-month 2026 net cash on debt principal and extinguishment was 585 while operating cash flow was 506 and cash fell by 438 to 1,038. The effect on leverage is that carrying total debt fell from 3,272 at year-end 2025 to 2,799 and total debt to company-defined Adjusted EBITDA was 3.28x on the last-twelve-month figure of 853. The mechanism for creditors is as follows. Replacing convertible notes with coupons of 3.50% and below by secured notes at 6.750% to 7.750% raises fixed interest; the accepted base puts stated coupons on outstanding debt at about 195 a year against last-twelve-month cash interest of 170. It lengthens maturities, since the earliest remaining maturity is the 229 million 2027 convertible notes. It adds secured claims that share first-priority liens with the revolver, while the remaining convertible notes are unsecured and structurally subordinated. Convertible notes retired for cash above principal convert dilution into a cash cost: cash paid, including accrued interest and fees, was 375 for 210 of principal in 2025 and 247 for 145 in 2026 (Calculations), with extinguishment losses of 165 and 102 equal to the difference to carrying value. Shares were also issued in settlement: 0.9 million on the 2027 notes and 4.5 million on the 2028 notes (Q3 10-Q page:14-15). The 2027 notes themselves became convertible for the quarter ending 2026-12-31 and the filing says conversion may be settled in cash, shares or a combination at the company's election (Q3 10-Q page:13), so the remaining unsecured claim carries a cash call that the company controls through the form of settlement. Recovery prospects appear here as a mechanic only: secured and unsecured claims have different positions against the same asset base, and the pack gives no valuation or recovery analysis.

Issuer: Wayfair Inc. (issuer id w), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, with Q3 2026 as the current period, FY2025 as the prior period and USD as the reporting currency. This module synthesises the fundamental credit view from the accepted financial base and the business and transaction context, using the upstream handoffs only, and gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion. The evidence cutoff is 2026-11-05.
## Sources
### Issuer sources behind the handoffs
This module reads no new source text; every figure comes from the handoffs below, which were checked against these pinned files.
| Source name | sha256 |
### Context file
| Source name | sha256 | Role |
| context | e3b6fe003758c2152693bc3785d916a8d51266f353efa91b71daa0110cb48520 | Run settings only; not issuer evidence |
### Supplied handoffs
| Module | sha256 | What this module takes from it |
| CP-0 | 9ba2d9c1e2e60174eaacd93db71cc6938042323a45533114c80ae7273f5486a5 | Source limits: no executed legal documents, covenant ratio, guarantor list, ratings or market data |
| CP-1 | 8232ff967a14f3da33fdcbbd5e43b820265a70b6cbcc48e608407bb2c6fd17ec | Financial base: statements, debt schedule, leverage, cover, liquidity, cash flow |
| CP-1A | 1853762b5adae9ef3371bf0fa46be49dcaed340fc5da9c9072e41691e813cc31 | Business model, ownership and control, transaction and liability-management history |
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Wayfair is a stronger credit than two years ago, with total debt to Adjusted EBITDA at 3.28x against 6.88x in FY2024, but it remains a thin-margin, demand-sensitive retailer whose leverage looks moderate only on company-defined earnings. | Medium | Covenant terms, ratings and executed debt documents are not supplied, and Adjusted EBITDA adds back equity compensation, so headroom and downside cannot be measured precisely. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt fell to 2,799 million while last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA rose to 853 million, cutting net debt to Adjusted EBITDA to 1.99x. | Deleveraging is real and mostly earnings-driven, which supports debt-service capacity. | High |

| Cash and investments of 1,098 million plus 418 million of undrawn revolver compare with 229 million of convertible notes due in 2027 and no other maturity before 2029. | Near-term refinancing risk is low; the open point is the form of settlement of the 2027 convertible notes. | Medium |

| Adjusted EBITDA adds back 293 million of equity compensation and related taxes; on operating income plus depreciation and amortization, total debt is 5.10x. | The reported leverage understates risk if equity pay is a real cost, and operating income covers net interest only 1.81x. | Medium |

| Stated coupons on 2,829 million of principal total about 195 million a year, above last-twelve-month cash interest of 170 million. | Interest burden is rising as low-coupon convertibles are replaced by 6.750% to 7.750% secured notes, so cover depends on continued earnings growth. | Medium |

| Founders hold 67.4% of voting power at year-end 2025 and secured notes make up 91.9% of principal. | Control and claim ranking favour secured holders and founders; protection against distributions rests on indentures that are not supplied. | Medium |
### Credit view

Wayfair Inc. is a better credit than it was two years ago, but it is still a thin-margin, discretionary-demand retailer whose leverage looks moderate only on management's own earnings measure. The strongest support is deleveraging: total debt fell to USD 2,799 million and total debt to Adjusted EBITDA to 3.28x from 6.88x in FY2024, with USD 1,098 million of cash and investments, an undrawn revolver and no maturity before September 2027. The weakest point is earnings quality: Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 293 million of equity compensation, and on operating income plus depreciation and amortization the ratio is 5.10x. What decides the outcome is whether U.S. order growth keeps converting into earnings faster than fixed interest is rising.
### Key findings

First, Wayfair has cut its debt and raised its earnings at the same time. Carrying total debt is USD 2,799 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 3,118 million at 2024-12-31, while last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is USD 853 million against USD 453 million in FY2024 [CP-1 handoff, leverage and metrics tables]. Total debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 3.28x and net debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 1.99x (Documentary Fact for the inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the improvement being earnings-led, since debt fell 10.2% and Adjusted EBITDA rose 88.3%).

Second, liquidity is ample against the visible maturities. Wayfair holds USD 1,038 million of cash and USD 60 million of short-term investments, has USD 418 million of undrawn revolver after letters of credit, and owes USD 229 million of convertible notes in September 2027 and USD 800 million of secured notes in October 2029 [CP-1 handoff, liquidity and maturity tables]. Cash and investments cover the 2027 principal 4.8 times (Calculations). The remaining unsecured notes are convertible during the quarter ending 2026-12-31 with an if-converted excess over principal of USD 141 million, and the company may settle in cash, shares or both, so the cash call is within its control [CP-1 handoff, debt schedule; CP-1A handoff, transaction summary] (Documentary Fact).

Third, the quality of the earnings measure decides how comfortable the leverage is. Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 293 million of equity-based compensation and related taxes over the last twelve months, which is 34.3% of Adjusted EBITDA, and the company also paid USD 77 million of tax on net share settlement and USD 60 million of buybacks through financing in nine months 2026 [CP-1 handoff, definition review]. On operating income plus depreciation and amortization of USD 549 million, total debt is 5.10x and net debt 3.10x; operating income of USD 283 million covers net interest expense of USD 156 million 1.81x (Calculations) (Analyst Interpretation).

Fourth, the cost of debt is rising even as the balance falls. Wayfair issued four fixed-rate secured series totalling USD 2,600 million since October 2024 and retired convertible notes with coupons of 3.50% and below, so stated coupons on USD 2,829 million of principal now total about USD 195 million a year against last-twelve-month cash interest of USD 170 million; Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 5.02x and run-rate coupons 4.36x [CP-1 handoff, interest cover; CP-1A handoff, transaction summary] (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation).

Fifth, the business is volume-led and U.S.-concentrated. The U.S. was 88% of FY2025 net revenue, Q3 2026 orders delivered rose to 11.0 million from 9.8 million while average order value fell to USD 311 from USD 317, and International Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of USD 54 million in nine months 2026 against U.S. earnings of USD 683 million [CP-1A handoff, Company and operating model; CP-1 handoff, segments] (Documentary Fact). Negative working capital, with accounts payable of USD 1,213 million against inventories of USD 89 million, funds operations and would reverse in a volume decline; nine-month 2026 operating cash flow included a working-capital inflow of USD 64 million against an outflow of USD 76 million a year earlier [CP-1 handoff, cash flow reading].

Sixth, control and creditor protection rest on documents the pack does not contain. The co-founders and affiliates held 67.4% of voting power and 18.3% of the economic interest at year-end 2025, Class B stock is 15.3% of combined shares against a 10% automatic conversion level, no dividend has ever been paid, and no priming, uptiering, drop-down or distribution evidence was found, but the indentures that would show capacity are not supplied [CP-1A handoff, ownership and governance table] (Documentary Fact; absence in the pack is not a finding of absence).
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. The first strength is deleveraging with earnings growth: last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 853 million is up from USD 743 million in FY2025 and USD 453 million in FY2024, and total debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 3.28x from 4.40x and 6.88x [CP-1 handoff] (Documentary Fact). The second is liquidity: USD 1,098 million of cash and short-term investments and USD 418 million of undrawn revolver exceed the USD 229 million due before 2029, which cash and investments alone cover 4.8 times (Calculations), and last-twelve-month free cash flow is USD 476 million, 55.8% of Adjusted EBITDA [CP-1 handoff] (Documentary Fact; the multiple is Analyst Interpretation). The third is a longer maturity profile: the 2026 and 2028 convertible notes are gone, the earliest remaining maturity is USD 229 million in September 2027, and the secured notes mature in 2029, 2030, 2032 and 2034 [CP-1 handoff, maturity table] (Documentary Fact). The fourth is repeat demand and growth: repeat customers placed 80.0% of Q3 2026 orders and net revenue rose 9.7% in the quarter, which supports revenue durability [CP-1A handoff; CP-1 handoff] (Documentary Fact; the release KPIs are management-calculated). The fifth is market access: the secured notes carry fair values between 98.9% and 102.9% of principal at 2026-09-30 (CP-1 handoff, debt schedule), consistent with continued access to secured debt markets (Analyst Interpretation).

Weaknesses. The first weakness is thin and adjusted earnings: net income over the last twelve months is a loss of USD 160 million, operating income plus depreciation and amortization is USD 549 million against Adjusted EBITDA of USD 853 million, and the stockholders' deficit is USD 2,804 million [CP-1 handoff] (Documentary Fact). The second is rising fixed interest, as set out in the fourth key finding, which leaves less room if earnings slip [CP-1 handoff; CP-1A handoff] (Analyst Interpretation). The third is demand and concentration risk: a discretionary category, 88% U.S. revenue, a loss-making International segment and a single small-parcel carrier [CP-1A handoff, Company and operating model] (Documentary Fact). The fourth is working-capital and seasonality sensitivity: first-quarter operating cash flow was negative in both years printed, and the 2026 working-capital inflow may not repeat [CP-1 handoff] (Analyst Interpretation). The fifth is that the claim stack is secured-heavy: secured notes are 91.9% of principal and share first-priority liens with the revolver, so the unsecured convertible notes rank behind them and structurally behind subsidiary liabilities, which matters for any loss given default analysis that later modules perform (mechanic only) [CP-1 handoff; CP-1A handoff] (Documentary Fact). The sixth is control and information: founder voting control, no covenant ratio reported, no ratings and no guidance mean that downside protection cannot be measured (Insufficient Information; the missing datapoints are the covenant definition and reported ratio, executed indentures, the proxy statement and ratings, as set out in Gaps).
### Credit assessment
| Item | Statement | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Assessment | Improving credit profile with moderate financial risk on company-defined earnings and high business risk from discretionary demand, thin margins and founder control; the view is sensitive to the treatment of equity compensation | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, cover and liquidity figures; CP-1A business model, ownership and liability-management rows |

| Thesis | Wayfair has used earnings growth and cash to cut debt and extend maturities, which supports its credit profile, but fixed interest is rising and earnings quality and covenant capacity are only partly observable | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | As above |

| Confidence reason | Below High because no covenant ratio, ratings, executed indentures or guidance are supplied, and the CP-1A readiness judgment for this module is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Not applicable | Medium | CP-0 and CP-1A limits |
### Credit metrics used

| Adjusted EBITDA, USD million | 453 | 743 | 853 | CP-1 |

| Adjusted EBITDA / cash interest, x | 7.19 | 5.35 | 5.02 | CP-1 |
| Free cash flow, USD million | 83 | 329 | 476 | CP-1 |
| Operating income / interest expense, net, x | Not meaningful | 0.14 | 1.81 | Calculated here |
| Cash and short-term investments, USD million | 1,372 | 1,542 | 1,098 | CP-1 |
| Undrawn revolver, USD million | Not supplied | 406 | 418 | CP-1 |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Category |

| Discretionary U.S. demand | 88% of revenue is U.S.; volume-led growth with falling order value depends on advertising efficiency | A demand slowdown cuts earnings faster than debt, raising leverage and cutting cover from 5.02x | Material | Analyst Interpretation |

| Earnings quality | Adjusted EBITDA adds back equity compensation and related taxes of USD 293 million; share-settlement tax and buybacks are paid in cash outside free cash flow | Leverage is 5.10x on unadjusted earnings; cash after dilution management is lower than free cash flow | Material | Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation |

| Rising fixed interest and refinancing | Coupons of 6.750% to 7.750% replaced convertibles of 3.50% and below; run-rate coupons about USD 195 million | Cover falls to 4.36x on run-rate coupons; USD 2,600 million of secured notes mature from 2029 and must be refinanced at market | Material | Analyst Interpretation |

| Working-capital reversal | Accounts payable USD 1,213 million against inventories USD 89 million; 2026 inflow of USD 64 million | A volume decline or tighter supplier terms would consume cash | Material | Analyst Interpretation |

| Covenant and document opacity | Revolver test of no more than 4.0 to 1.0 on a defined EBITDA that is not supplied; indentures not supplied | Headroom, guarantor coverage and distribution capacity cannot be measured | Material | Insufficient Information |

| Founder control | 67.4% voting power with 18.3% economic interest | Equity holders can approve mergers and charter changes; creditor protection depends on indenture capacity | Material | Documentary Fact |

| 2027 convertible notes | USD 229 million, convertible in the quarter ending 2026-12-31, settlement form at the company's election | Cash or dilution call; cash on hand is ample relative to principal | Minor | Documentary Fact |

| International losses and contingent claims | International Adjusted EBITDA loss of USD 54 million in nine months 2026; customs matter and litigation accruals not quantified | Drag on earnings; small unquantified claims | Minor | Documentary Fact |
## Calculations

| Liquidity | 1,098 cash and investments + 418 undrawn revolver | 1,516 |
## Gaps

| Covenant definition of Consolidated EBITDA and the reported senior secured leverage ratio are not supplied; only the 4.0 to 1.0 level and a compliance statement are known | Headroom against the one named test cannot be measured, so downside cannot be sized | Assessment, weakness on information | High | Obtain the credit agreement and compliance certificate |

| No credit ratings, market prices or peer data | No external credit view; conversion likelihood of the 2027 notes cannot be judged without a cutoff share price | Assessment confidence | Medium | Supply dated market data and ratings |
| No management guidance | No forward earnings view for interest cover or covenant projection | Cover and leverage outlook | Medium | None in the pack |

| 2026 proxy statement and use of proceeds for the 2029 and 2032 issues are not supplied | Board independence, related-party terms and the link between new secured debt and convertible retirements are only partly known | Governance, capital structure change | Medium | Obtain the proxy statement and offering releases |

| Springing maturity trigger of the revolver and current margin are not printed | A springing maturity could move the 2030 revolver date forward | Maturity profile | Medium | Obtain the credit agreement |

| Canada Border Services Agency matter described in the 10-K only; litigation accruals not quantified | Small contingent claims with unknown status after year end | Contingent claims | Medium | Check later filings |
| Q4 2025 stand-alone quarter and Q3 2025 balance sheet are derived or not supplied | Discrete-quarter analysis is derived, not printed | Trend analysis | Low | Label as derived |
| Release superlatives and KPIs are management claims | They cannot be tested with the pack | Strengths on demand | Low | Treat as attributed |

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a better credit view than the Medium-confidence synthesis is that Q3 2026 operating income of 106 is up from 38, Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA margin of 6.9% is up from 6.7%, orders delivered rose 12.2%, last-twelve-month free cash flow of 476 is 55.8% of Adjusted EBITDA, and liquidity of 1,516 including the revolver is large against 229 due in 2027. What would make that case win: last-twelve-month net income, a loss of 160, turning positive as extinguishment losses fall away, unadjusted leverage falling below 5.10x as operating income grows, and the 2027 notes settling without a large cash call.

The downside chain, with observable triggers, starts with a slowdown in U.S. demand (initiating condition). The first operational break would be falling orders delivered or lower average order value, which the release reports each quarter, forcing more advertising per order. The financial transmission is lower Adjusted EBITDA and a reversal of the 64 working-capital inflow as payables of 1,213 unwind against inventories of 89. The consequences are lower cash than the 1,038 held, less cover than 5.02x, and higher leverage, with the arithmetic reference points that LTM Adjusted EBITDA at the FY2025 level of 743 gives total debt of 3.77x and at the FY2024 level of 453 gives 6.18x (Calculations; these are reference levels, not forecasts). Refinancing then matters from 2029, when 800 of secured notes mature at market rates. Triggers to watch: quarterly orders and average order value, Adjusted EBITDA margin against 6.9%, cash against 1,038, the settlement election on the 2027 notes, and covenant certificates when obtained.
